patients.summary: A 25-year-old teacher with myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine and a history of gestational hypertension joins in 2022. Her second pregnancy ends in severe preeclampsia at 34 weeks with induced delivery, then a delayed postpartum preeclampsia five weeks later, managed by obstetrics without magnesium because of her myasthenia.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 yo F, elementary school teacher, establishing care.

Myasthenia gravis: diagnosed before she moved here, managed by an outside neurology group that she will keep seeing about once a year. On pyridostigmine 60 mg three times a day. Feels well controlled. Denies droopy lids, double vision, trouble swallowing or chewing, or shortness of breath. No crises, no hospital stays for it. No prior surgery.

OB: G1P1. One pregnancy, delivered at term in 2021. Developed gestational hypertension in that pregnancy, monitored to delivery, no complications; BP back to normal afterward and never treated since.

Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg TID.
Allergies: none to drugs.
FHx: mother had preeclampsia in pregnancy. A maternal cousin has lupus.
SHx: never smoker. Drinks a glass of wine socially, a few times a month. One toddler at home. Teaches second grade.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Well appearing. No ptosis at rest or with sustained upgaze for 60 seconds, EOM full without diplopia. Facial strength symmetric. Neck flexion and shoulder abduction 5/5 with repetition. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric.

Assessment / plan:
1. Myasthenia gravis, stable on pyridostigmine. Neurology continues to direct care. Will request their most recent note. Reviewed that some common drugs can worsen MG and asked her to remind any prescriber.
2. History of gestational hypertension. BP acceptable on a single reading today. Discussed that it matters for future pregnancies and long term; check yearly.
3. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees. Last cervical cytology was with her prenatal care in 2021; records requested from her prior office. Flu and COVID vaccines when the fall supply arrives.

Return for a physical next summer.

documents.title: Your recent bloodwork

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group, follow-up visit of 11/17/2022.

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Tremblay today for her yearly myasthenia gravis visit. She has had a quiet year. No ptosis, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia or breathing trouble, and she is managing a full teaching load without fatigue beyond the ordinary.

Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg three times daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Examination: alert, fluent speech. No ptosis after sustained upgaze. Extraocular movements full. Facial, bulbar and neck strength normal. Limb strength 5/5 throughout without fatigability on repeated testing. Reflexes symmetric.

Impression: myasthenia gravis, clinically stable on pyridostigmine.

Plan: continue pyridostigmine 60 mg three times daily. Return in a year, sooner with any weakness. She knows to call before starting a new antibiotic or any drug flagged for MG.

Thank you for allowing me to share in her care.

26 yo F for her yearly exam, a week before school starts.

Interval: no illnesses. MG unchanged, still pyridostigmine 60 mg TID, saw neurology last November and is due again this fall. No weakness, no diplopia, swallowing fine. Not planning another pregnancy this year.

Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, wine occasionally. Exercises with a stroller walk most evenings.
PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: vitals as recorded, BP normal. No ptosis, EOM full. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Strength full and symmetric. Skin clear.

A/P:
- MG, stable. Neurology to continue.
- History of gestational hypertension, BP normal today.
- Prevention: cervical cytology due 2024 (normal 2021). CBC today. Flu and updated COVID vaccine at a nurse visit in October.

One year.

documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Visit date 11/14/2023.

Ms. Tremblay returns for routine follow-up of myasthenia gravis. Another stable year: no ocular, bulbar or respiratory symptoms and no exacerbations. Takes pyridostigmine 60 mg TID with no GI side effects to speak of.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: no ptosis or diplopia with prolonged gaze testing. Normal facial and neck flexor strength. Limbs 5/5 without fatigue on repetition. Gait normal.

Assessment: myasthenia gravis, stable.
Plan: no change; pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. Follow up in 12 months. If she considers another pregnancy, she should let us know beforehand so we can review her medications.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 yo here for yearly physical and cervical screening.

Doing well. Busy summer with her little one. MG stable, no weakness or visual symptoms; neurology visit last November unchanged, next one this fall. Takes pyridostigmine 60 mg three times daily, refills through us.

NKDA. Never smoker, rare alcohol.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: BP normal, other vitals as charted. No ptosis, EOM full. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. No edema.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap sent (last one normal in 2021). Flu shot in October. Labs not needed this year.
- MG: stable, continue current dose.
- Hx gestational HTN: normotensive.

See her next summer.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Date of service: 11/19/2024.

Re: Zoe Tremblay, DOB 4/22/1997

Seen for annual review of myasthenia gravis. She reports no fluctuating weakness, no ptosis, no diplopia and no chewing or swallowing fatigue. Pyridostigmine 60 mg three times a day continues to suit her. NKDA.

On examination she has no ptosis after one minute of upgaze, full eye movements, normal speech, and full strength in neck flexors, deltoids, hip flexors and grip, without decrement on repetition.

Impression: myasthenia gravis, in good control on symptomatic therapy alone.

Recommendations: continue pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. Annual follow-up. We again talked about a future pregnancy; she would like to try in the next year and will contact us before then so we can plan.

documents.title: Mestinon and pregnancy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, we are hoping to try for a second baby later this year. Is it ok to stay on my Mestinon? I took it the whole time last pregnancy but I want to double check. Thanks, Zoe

documents.title: RE: Mestinon and pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Pyridostigmine is generally continued through pregnancy, and stopping it would carry more risk for your MG than staying on it. Please let your neurologist know your plans too, since they will want to coordinate with obstetrics. We can go over the rest of preconception planning at your physical this summer.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 yo F, yearly exam. She plans to start trying for a second pregnancy this fall.

MG: stable, pyridostigmine 60 mg TID, no symptoms. Neurology aware of pregnancy plans per patient.
Prior pregnancy: gestational hypertension, term delivery.
NKDA. Never smoker; drinks only occasionally and will stop when trying.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: vitals as recorded, BP normal. Weight stable. No ptosis. Thyroid normal. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Plan
- Preconception: start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily now. Continue pyridostigmine. Once pregnant, let us know and we will get her to obstetrics early, given her MG and prior gestational hypertension. CBC and TSH today.
- Pap up to date (2024 normal).
- Flu vaccine this fall.

Next physical in a year or sooner with news.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Positive home test 10/7. LMP 9/4/25, regular cycles, so about 5 weeks today; EDD by dates 6/11/26. Mild fatigue and breast tenderness. No bleeding, no pain. Taking prenatal vitamin since August and pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. No MG symptoms.

O: BP normal, vitals as charted. Well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender. Urine hCG positive in office.

A/P: Intrauterine pregnancy not yet confirmed, about 5 weeks by LMP. Second pregnancy; first had gestational hypertension. Myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine.
- Referral to obstetrics placed, flagged for early high-risk scheduling.
- Continue prenatal vitamin and pyridostigmine.
- She will update neurology this week.
- Nausea and bleeding precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Neurology Letter: Pregnancy Counseling
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Visit of 10/28/2025.

Ms. Tremblay is now about 7 weeks pregnant and came in to plan her myasthenia care through pregnancy and delivery. She remains symptom free on pyridostigmine 60 mg three times a day. Exam today is normal, with no ptosis, diplopia or fatigable weakness.

Recommendations, shared with her and copied to obstetrics and primary care:
1. Continue pyridostigmine 60 mg TID throughout pregnancy and the postpartum period. Breastfeeding is compatible.
2. Several medications can worsen myasthenia and should be avoided or used only after discussion with us, most importantly magnesium sulfate, as well as aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones and macrolides. If magnesium would otherwise be indicated, please call neurology; alternatives exist.
3. Labor itself is usually unaffected, but she should alert the delivery team to her diagnosis on arrival.
4. We will see her postpartum or sooner with any weakness.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics and gynecology practice. Prenatal visit, 11/25/2025.

G2P1, 11 weeks 5 days by LMP of 9/4/2025, EDD 6/11/2026. Seen on referral from primary care.

So far this pregnancy has been uneventful. She is taking her prenatal vitamins every day and has no concerns today. Her main question was about the coming flu season and how best to protect herself and the baby.

PMH: myasthenia gravis, followed by neurology (their counseling letter reviewed). Gestational hypertension in her first pregnancy, which went to term and delivered without problems.
PSH: none.
Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO TID.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother had preeclampsia; a maternal cousin with lupus.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol since conception.

Vitals within normal limits, BP normal. General exam unremarkable.

Plan:
- Inactivated influenza vaccine given today; safe at any point in pregnancy. Discussed that Tdap is recommended between 27 and 36 weeks to pass protection to the newborn; plan for it at the early third-trimester visit.
- Neurology recommendations noted on her chart, including avoidance of magnesium sulfate.
- Routine prenatal care; return in 4 weeks.

cc: primary care

Outside obstetrics and gynecology practice. Prenatal visit 3/19/2026.

G2P1 at 28w0d. Feeling well, good fetal movement, no headaches, no visual change, no swelling. Myasthenia quiet on pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. Prenatal vitamin daily.

BP normal today. Fundal height appropriate. Fetal heart tones present and normal. No edema.

Tdap given today, left deltoid, for newborn pertussis protection.

Plan: routine visits every 2 weeks from here. Reviewed warning signs of preeclampsia given her history (severe headache, visual change, right upper abdominal pain, sudden swelling) and to go to labor and delivery or the ED if they occur.

Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Severe headache and flashing lights in vision

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. Seen 4/30/2026, arrived 07:40.

CC: severe headache, flashing lights in vision.

HPI: 29 yo G2P1 at 34w0d (EDD 6/11/26) with myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine and gestational hypertension in her prior pregnancy. Headache began yesterday, now severe and not relieved by acetaminophen at home; since last night she sees flashing lights. Pressures had been normal at prenatal visits, most recently in early April per patient. Good fetal movement. No bleeding, no leakage of fluid, no contractions.

Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO TID; prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: none.
FHx: mother with preeclampsia; maternal cousin with SLE.
SH: teacher, never smoker, no alcohol in pregnancy.

Exam: BP 158/102. Uncomfortable, photophobic. 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities. DTRs brisk with clonus at the ankles. No focal weakness, no ptosis. Gravid abdomen, nontender, including RUQ. Fetal heart tracing reassuring on monitor per L&D nurse.

Results: UA protein 2+. Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (elevated). AST 70 U/L, ALT 80 U/L (elevated). Platelets 180 K/uL. Hgb 12.0 g/dL. LDH 171 U/L, within range.

MDM: new hypertension with headache, visual symptoms, proteinuria, rising creatinine and transaminases at 34 weeks: preeclampsia with severe features. Platelets and LDH do not suggest HELLP. OB at bedside; patient's neurology plan on file advises against magnesium sulfate. Neurology called and agrees magnesium should be avoided; levetiracetam recommended for seizure prophylaxis.

Dx: severe preeclampsia without HELLP features, 34 weeks.
Disposition: admitted to labor and delivery for stabilization and delivery.

medications.sig: 500 mg by mouth twice daily until 24 hours after delivery
medications.reason: seizure prophylaxis, magnesium avoided in myasthenia gravis

medications.sig: 5 to 10 mg IV as needed for severe-range blood pressure

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 4/30/2026, discharged 5/3/2026.

Admitting diagnosis: preeclampsia with severe features at 34w0d, no HELLP features. Background: myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine; gestational hypertension in first pregnancy.

Course: admitted from the ED. Magnesium sulfate was not used because of myasthenia gravis, per neurology; levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily was given for seizure prophylaxis and continued for 24 hours after delivery. Severe-range pressures were treated with IV hydralazine as needed. Labor was induced with oxytocin and she had a vaginal delivery of a liveborn infant on 5/1/2026 at 03:12, at 34w1d. Headache and visual symptoms resolved after delivery. No myasthenic weakness at any point; pyridostigmine continued on schedule. Postpartum pressures settled into the 130s to low 140s over 80s to 90s without oral agents.

Labs at discharge (5/3): creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, AST 45 U/L, ALT 52 U/L, platelets 168 K/uL.

Discharge medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO TID; prenatal vitamin daily. No antihypertensive.
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: home BP twice daily with the provided cuff. Return for BP 160/110 or higher, headache, visual change, RUQ pain, shortness of breath. OB BP check within a week. Notify neurology of any weakness.

cc: primary care, neurology

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home, ID verified, consents to video.

Postpartum day 4. Admitted 4/30 from the ED at 34 weeks with severe preeclampsia without HELLP features (BP 158/102, protein 2+, Cr 1.2, AST 70, ALT 80, plt 180). Magnesium avoided because of her MG; levetiracetam and IV hydralazine; induced and delivered vaginally 5/1. Discharge labs improved (Cr 1.0, AST 45, ALT 52, plt 168). Home yesterday on no BP medication. ED record and discharge summary reviewed.

Today: headache gone, vision normal, no RUQ pain, no shortness of breath. Mild leg swelling improving. Home cuff readings since discharge 126-138 / 80-88. MG: no weakness, swallowing normal, on pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. Sleeping in pieces with a newborn but mood good; PHQ-2 0.

Exam (video): comfortable, speaking in full sentences, no ptosis, normal facial movement.

A/P
1. Severe preeclampsia without HELLP features, delivered. Pressures acceptable off medication. Keep checking twice daily. Any reading 160/110 or higher, or a headache, vision change or upper belly pain, go to L&D/ED directly; risk persists for several weeks after delivery. OB BP check later this week as planned.
2. Myasthenia gravis: stable; continue pyridostigmine. Neurology to see postpartum.
3. Prior gestational hypertension and now preeclampsia: long-term cardiovascular risk is higher; yearly BP, lipids and glucose here.

Physical with us in late summer or early fall.

documents.title: BP log
documents.author: patient

events.reason: Headache, visual disturbance, right upper abdominal pain

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 6/4/2026.

Chief complaint: headache with visual disturbance and pain under the right ribs.

History: 29 yo, 34 days after a vaginal delivery at 34 weeks for severe preeclampsia (5/1/2026). Home pressures had been in the 120s-130s. Today developed a headache, spots in her vision and right upper quadrant pain. Known myasthenia gravis, well controlled on pyridostigmine.

Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO TID, prenatal vitamin 1 tab daily. NKDA. PSH: none. FHx: mother had preeclampsia; maternal cousin with SLE. SH: teacher, never smoker, no current alcohol.

Exam: BP 160/110. Alert, oriented, no ptosis. Lungs clear. RUQ tender without guarding. Lower extremities with 2+ edema. Reflexes brisk.

Data: urine protein 3+. Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. Platelets 110 K/uL. AST 70 U/L, ALT 65 U/L. LDH 186 U/L, no hemolysis pattern.

Assessment: delayed postpartum preeclampsia with severe features, no HELLP features.

Course here: OB consulted. Magnesium sulfate was raised for seizure prophylaxis; after a call with on-call neurology it was not given because of her myasthenia, and levetiracetam was started instead. IV hydralazine for BP. Admitted to the postpartum unit under OB.

documents.title: Postpartum Readmission Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, postpartum unit. Admission 6/4/2026 to 6/7/2026.

Diagnosis: postpartum preeclampsia with severe features, without HELLP features, 34 days after delivery.
Comorbidity: myasthenia gravis.

Hospital course: magnesium sulfate withheld in view of myasthenia gravis, on neurology's advice. Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily for 24 hours. IV hydralazine for severe-range pressures overnight, then nifedipine ER 30 mg daily started with good control. Headache, visual symptoms and RUQ pain resolved by hospital day 2. Strength remained normal throughout.

Discharge labs (6/7): platelets 142 K/uL, AST 44 U/L, ALT 41 U/L.

Discharge medications: nifedipine ER 30 mg PO daily (new); pyridostigmine 60 mg PO TID; prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: OB in 1 week for BP check, then her postpartum visit. Continue home BP log. Return precautions given.

cc: primary care, neurology

documents.title: Back in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I was readmitted last week, my pressure went up again with a headache. They put me on nifedipine. OB is following me. Do I need to see you too?

documents.title: RE: Back in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm sorry you had to go back in. I have the hospital records now. OB is the right team to adjust the nifedipine over the next few weeks, so no separate visit with me right now. Let's keep the fall physical on the calendar so we can look at your blood pressure together once things settle.

documents.title: Obstetrics Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics and gynecology practice. Postpartum visit, 7/9/2026, about 10 weeks after delivery and 5 weeks after readmission for postpartum preeclampsia.

Feeling well. No headaches or visual symptoms. Home BP 110s-120s/70s on nifedipine ER 30 mg. MG stable on pyridostigmine.

BP 116/74 today. Exam: no edema; abdomen soft; perineum healed.

Plan:
- Stop nifedipine. Check home BP a few times a week for a month and call for readings at or above 140/90.
- Counseled that preeclampsia and prior gestational hypertension raise her long-term risk of hypertension and cardiovascular disease; she should have blood pressure checked at least yearly with primary care.
- Continue pyridostigmine; neurology aware.

Allergies: NKDA.
cc: primary care
